title: Systems Malfunctions, Fire & Startle Response

required_knowledge_points.title: Engine Power Loss — Fuel Starvation, Carburetor Icing, and Ignition Failures
required_knowledge_points.why: The DPE asks: 'What causes engine power loss?' The three primary killers are fuel starvation (fuel exists but can't reach the engine), carburetor icing (can happen on a 70°F day), and ignition failure (magnetos). The pilot who says 'ran out of gas' is describing fuel exhaustion — that's a planning failure. Fuel starvation is a mechanical/procedural failure with fuel still on board.
required_knowledge_points.knowledge: FUEL STARVATION vs. FUEL EXHAUSTION: Exhaustion = tanks are empty (planning failure). Starvation = fuel is on board but cannot reach the engine. Starvation causes: (1) Fuel selector on wrong tank (most common), (2) Blocked fuel vent creating vacuum that stops gravity flow, (3) Vapor lock — high temperature/altitude boils fuel in lines, creating gas bubbles the mechanical pump can't push through, (4) Uncoordinated flight unporting the fuel pickup in the tank. CARBURETOR ICING: occurs even on warm days (up to 70°F/21°C) with high humidity. Physics: air accelerates through the carburetor venturi → pressure drops (Bernoulli) → fuel vaporizes absorbing heat (latent heat of vaporization) → temperature inside carburetor throat drops up to 70°F → moisture freezes on the throttle valve → chokes air supply → gradual RPM loss. Symptoms: gradual RPM decrease (fixed pitch) or manifold pressure decrease (constant speed). Treatment: apply carb heat FULL (RPM will initially drop further as warm, less-dense air enters). Leave carb heat ON until RPM stabilizes and rises. IGNITION SYSTEM: dual magnetos are mechanically driven off the engine — they are INDEPENDENT of the electrical system. If the battery and alternator both fail, the engine continues running. Magneto failure: internal timing slip or drive gear failure → power loss or severe roughness. Single magneto failure = engine runs on remaining magneto with slight RPM drop. Both magnetos fail = complete engine stoppage. OIL SYSTEM: loss of oil pressure → metal-on-metal friction → piston rings fuse to cylinder walls → complete engine seizure within minutes.
required_knowledge_points.knowledge_formatted:
### Fuel Starvation vs. Fuel Exhaustion
| Condition | Definition | Cause |
|---|---|---|
| **Exhaustion** | Tanks are **empty** | Planning/ADM failure |
| **Starvation** | Fuel on board, can't reach engine | Selector wrong, vent blocked, vapor lock |

### Carburetor Icing
```
Air enters venturi → accelerates → pressure DROPS (Bernoulli)
→ Fuel vaporizes → absorbs heat (latent heat of vaporization)
→ Temperature drops up to 70°F inside carburetor throat
→ Moisture in air FREEZES on throttle valve
→ Chokes air supply → gradual RPM loss
```
**Can occur at ambient temps up to 70°F (21°C) with high humidity**

| Symptom | Fixed-Pitch Prop | Constant-Speed Prop |
|---|---|---|
| Icing indication | Gradual RPM decrease | Manifold pressure decrease |

**Treatment:** Full carb heat ON → initial RPM drop (expected) → RPM rises as ice melts

### Ignition System Independence
- Magnetos are **mechanically driven** off the engine
- **Independent** of battery/alternator
- Battery dead + alternator failed = **engine still runs**
- Single magneto failure = slight RPM drop, engine continues
- Both magnetos fail = engine stops

> ⚠️ **Checkride Trap:** 'If the alternator and battery both fail, does the engine quit?' NO. Magnetos are mechanically driven. The engine runs perfectly. You lose radios, lights, and instruments — not the engine.

required_knowledge_points.title: Pitot-Static System Malfunctions — Blocked Pitot, Blocked Static, and the 'Altimeter' Trap
required_knowledge_points.why: The DPE asks: 'What happens to your instruments if the pitot tube ices over?' If both the ram inlet AND drain hole freeze, the ASI acts like an ALTIMETER — it shows increasing airspeed as you climb, decreasing as you descend. A pilot who trusts this indication and pulls back to 'slow down' will stall the aircraft.
required_knowledge_points.knowledge: PITOT-STATIC SYSTEM: the ASI measures dynamic pressure (q = Total Pressure - Static Pressure). The pitot tube provides total pressure (PT). The static port provides static pressure (PS). BLOCKED PITOT (drain open): ram air stops entering → diaphragm pressure drops → ASI reads ZERO. Other instruments (altimeter, VSI) use static port only — they are unaffected. BLOCKED PITOT (drain closed — most dangerous): total pressure is TRAPPED in the line at the blockage altitude. If the aircraft CLIMBS: actual static pressure drops, but trapped PT stays the same. q = PT(trapped) - PS(lower) = LARGER q → ASI reads HIGHER. The ASI shows the aircraft SPEEDING UP as it climbs — acting exactly like an altimeter. If the pilot trusts this and pulls back to 'slow down,' they increase AOA toward stall while the ASI shows increasing speed. FATAL TRAP. If the aircraft DESCENDS: actual static pressure rises, q = PT(trapped) - PS(higher) = SMALLER q → ASI reads LOWER. BLOCKED STATIC PORT: all three instruments affected. Altimeter FREEZES at blockage altitude. VSI FREEZES at zero. ASI reads LOW in a climb (trapped static is higher than actual = less apparent q) and HIGH in a descent (trapped static lower than actual = more apparent q). ALTERNATE STATIC SOURCE: opens valve to cabin air. Cabin pressure is slightly LOWER than outside (venturi effect over fuselage). Result: altimeter reads slightly HIGH, ASI reads slightly HIGH, VSI shows momentary climb. EMERGENCY: if no alternate static exists, break the VSI glass face to vent cabin air into the static lines.
required_knowledge_points.knowledge_formatted:
### Pitot-Static Malfunction Summary
| Malfunction | ASI | Altimeter | VSI |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Pitot blocked (drain open)** | Drops to **ZERO** | Normal | Normal |
| **Pitot blocked (drain closed)** | Acts like **ALTIMETER** ↑climb ↑speed | Normal | Normal |
| **Static port blocked** | Low in climb, high in descent | **FREEZES** at blockage altitude | **FREEZES** at zero |
| **Alternate static open** | Reads slightly **HIGH** | Reads slightly **HIGH** | Momentary climb |

### The 'Altimeter' Trap (Pitot + Drain Blocked)
```
Pitot ices over (ram + drain) → total pressure TRAPPED

Climb: actual static drops → q = PT(trapped) - PS(lower) = BIG q
→ ASI shows INCREASING speed during climb ← DANGEROUS
→ Pilot pulls back to "slow down" → actually approaching stall
→ ASI keeps showing "fast" → pilot keeps pulling → STALL → FATAL

Descent: actual static rises → q = PT(trapped) - PS(higher) = SMALL q  
→ ASI shows DECREASING speed during descent
→ Pilot pushes nose down to "gain speed" → accelerates toward Vne
```

### Alternate Static Source Effects
- Cabin air is slightly **lower pressure** than outside (venturi effect)
- Altimeter: reads slightly **higher** than actual
- ASI: reads slightly **faster** than actual
- VSI: momentary climb indication, then stabilizes

> ⚠️ **Checkride Trap:** 'Your pitot tube and drain both ice over in a climb. What does the ASI show?' INCREASING SPEED — because it's acting like an altimeter. The pilot who trusts this indication will stall.

required_knowledge_points.title: In-Flight Fire — Electrical Load Shedding and Engine Fire Emergency Descent
required_knowledge_points.why: The DPE asks: 'What do you do if you smell burning plastic in the cockpit?' That's an electrical fire. Master Switch OFF — immediately. The engine keeps running (magnetos are independent). Then systematically shed loads to isolate the fault. An engine fire is different: cut the fuel, kill the mixture, and get the airplane on the ground NOW.
required_knowledge_points.knowledge: FIRE TRIANGLE: Heat + Fuel + Oxygen. In the sky, oxygen is abundant and cannot be removed. The pilot must eliminate HEAT (electrical fires) or FUEL (engine fires). ELECTRICAL FIRE: caused by short circuits, chafed wiring, or over-voltage conditions. Smell: burning plastic, ozone. Smoke: white/gray, from behind instrument panel. IMMEDIATE ACTION: Master Switch OFF (kills both alternator and battery). Engine continues running (magnetos are independent). Confirm fire is out. Load shedding: turn battery ON, then systematically turn individual breakers ON one at a time to isolate the faulty circuit. If smoke returns on any circuit, turn it OFF immediately. Retrieve only minimum avionics needed to land. VENTILATION: do NOT open windows carelessly — the low-pressure aerodynamic vortex outside the window acts as a vacuum, sucking flames and smoke across the pilot's face. Follow POH ventilation procedures specifically. ENGINE FIRE: IMMEDIATE ACTION: Mixture to idle cut-off → Fuel selector OFF → Fuel pump OFF. The engine will die. Execute emergency descent. POH-specific: some manufacturers prescribe high-speed dive (near Vne) to blow the fire out with slipstream. Others warn against fanning flames. Follow the POH. If fire breaches the cabin: exercise 91.3 emergency authority and put the aircraft on the ground ANYWHERE immediately — asphyxiation or structural failure is imminent. CABIN FIRE EXTINGUISHER: Halon or dry chemical. Point at the base of the fire. After discharge: ventilate the cabin immediately (Halon displaces oxygen and the chemicals are toxic in confined spaces).
required_knowledge_points.knowledge_formatted:
### Electrical Fire Procedure
```
1. Master Switch → OFF (kills heat source)
   ⚡ Engine keeps running — magnetos are independent
2. Confirm fire is OUT (smoke stops)
3. If ventilation needed → follow POH procedure
   ❌ Do NOT open window carelessly (venturi vacuum sucks flames)
4. LOAD SHEDDING:
   Battery → ON
   Turn breakers ON one at a time
   Smoke returns? → that circuit is the fault → OFF
   Retrieve only minimum avionics to land
```

### Engine Fire Procedure
```
1. Mixture → IDLE CUT-OFF (starve fuel)
2. Fuel Selector → OFF
3. Fuel Pump → OFF
4. Engine dies → execute EMERGENCY DESCENT
5. Follow POH for airspeed (some: high-speed dive; others: controlled)
6. LAND IMMEDIATELY
```

### Fire Triangle
| Element | Pilot Action |
|---|---|
| **Heat** | Electrical: Master Switch OFF |
| **Fuel** | Engine: Mixture cut-off, Fuel OFF |
| **Oxygen** | Cannot control in open atmosphere |

### Fire Extinguisher Use
- Point at **base** of fire (not the flames)
- After discharge: **ventilate** immediately (toxic fumes)
- Halon displaces oxygen — dangerous in confined cockpit

> ⚠️ **Checkride Trap:** 'You smell burning plastic. What do you do FIRST?' Master Switch OFF. Not 'check the breakers.' Not 'look for smoke.' OFF. The engine keeps running.

required_knowledge_points.title: Startle Response, Checklist Discipline, and the DECIDE Model
required_knowledge_points.why: The DPE simulates an emergency and watches your reaction. The startle response — the 'amygdala hijack' — freezes your brain for up to 30 seconds. At 1,000 fpm descent, 30 seconds = 500 feet of lost altitude with zero pilot input. The defense: pre-brief emergencies before takeoff so the brain has a pre-loaded script when the amygdala fires.
required_knowledge_points.knowledge: STARTLE RESPONSE: an involuntary physiological reaction to a sudden emergency. The amygdala bypasses the logical prefrontal cortex and triggers the sympathetic nervous system (fight/flight/freeze). Effects: cognitive paralysis for up to 30 seconds, tunnel vision, auditory exclusion, inappropriate motor responses (pulling back on the yoke when the engine quits — instinctively 'pulling away from the ground'). At 1,000 fpm descent, 30 seconds = 500 feet of altitude lost with zero pilot input. MITIGATION: pre-takeoff verbal briefing ('if the engine fails below 1,000 feet, I push the nose down and land straight ahead'). This pre-loads a script that short-circuits the freeze response. THE PPLA FRAMEWORK: Pitch to horizon (or Vg) → Power to appropriate setting → Level the wings → Analyze. Physical, rote actions that stabilize the aircraft and buy time for the prefrontal cortex to come back online. CHECKLIST DISCIPLINE: working memory holds 4-7 items. Under stress (cortisol/adrenaline), this capacity drops further. The printed checklist is an external cognitive aid. DO-VERIFY vs. READ-DO: Do-Verify = perform rote memory flow, then verify against checklist. Read-Do = read each step, then perform it. Do-Verify for time-critical emergencies. Read-Do for slower-developing malfunctions. CHECKLIST MISIDENTIFICATION: misdiagnosing the problem → running the wrong checklist → creating a new emergency. Example: rough running from carb ice → pilot diagnoses engine failure → executes shutdown checklist → now has an actual dead engine. Verify symptoms against gauges before committing to irreversible actions. THE DECIDE MODEL: Detect the change → Estimate the need to react → Choose a desirable outcome → Identify actions → Do the action → Evaluate the effect.
required_knowledge_points.knowledge_formatted:
### The Startle Response
```
Sudden emergency → amygdala fires
→ Bypasses prefrontal cortex (logic)
→ Triggers fight/flight/FREEZE
→ Cognitive paralysis for up to 30 SECONDS
→ At 1,000 fpm descent = 500 ft of uncontrolled flight
```

### Dangerous Startle Reactions
| Reaction | Why It's Fatal |
|---|---|
| **Pulling back on yoke** | Instinct to 'pull away from ground' → stalls the aircraft |
| **Cognitive freeze** | No pilot input → aircraft descends uncontrolled |
| **Tunnel vision** | Fixates on one warning → misses stall horn |
| **Denial** | 'It'll clear up' → wastes critical altitude |

### Pre-Takeoff Briefing (The Antidote)
- "If the engine fails below [X] feet: push nose down, land straight ahead"
- Pre-loads a **script** → short-circuits the freeze response
- The brain executes the pre-loaded action BEFORE the amygdala fully hijacks

### PPLA Framework
| Step | Action | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| **P** | Pitch to horizon / Vg | Stabilize flight path |
| **P** | Power to appropriate setting | Configure thrust |
| **L** | Level the wings | Stop turning |
| **A** | Analyze the situation | Engage logical brain |

### Checklist Methodology
| Method | When | How |
|---|---|---|
| **Do-Verify** | Time-critical emergency | Perform rote flow → verify against checklist |
| **Read-Do** | Slow-developing malfunction | Read step → perform → read next step |

### The DECIDE Model
**D**etect → **E**stimate → **C**hoose → **I**dentify → **D**o → **E**valuate

> ⚠️ **Checkride Trap:** The DPE is watching your REACTION TIME, not your technical knowledge. A 3-second response to engine failure = pass. A 15-second freeze = concern. A brief pre-takeoff emergency briefing is the single most effective mitigation.

lesson_overview:
## Systems Malfunctions, Fire, and the Startle Response — Managing Chaos in the Cockpit

This lesson covers the systems failures, fires, and human-factors challenges that constitute the emergency operations dimension of the private pilot checkride. Every scenario tested here shares a common thread: the pilot who maintains aircraft control and follows a systematic process will survive. The pilot who panics, fixates, or guesses will not.

**Engine power loss has three primary causes, each with a distinct signature and remedy.** Fuel starvation — the most common — means fuel is on board but cannot reach the engine, typically because the fuel selector is on the wrong tank, a fuel vent is blocked, or vapor lock has formed in the lines. Carburetor icing is the stealthiest killer, capable of forming on days as warm as 70°F when humidity is high. The venturi effect combined with the latent heat of fuel vaporization drops the temperature inside the carburetor throat by up to 70°F, freezing moisture onto the throttle valve and choking the air supply. The fix is full carburetor heat — accepting the initial RPM drop as warm, less-dense air enters. The dual magneto ignition system is independent of the electrical system entirely. If the battery and alternator both fail, the engine continues running perfectly. Magneto failure manifests as roughness (single mag) or complete stoppage (both mags).

**Pitot-static system malfunctions produce instrument readings that can actively deceive the pilot into stalling the aircraft.** When the pitot tube and its drain hole both freeze over, the total pressure in the line becomes trapped. As the aircraft climbs, the actual static pressure drops — but the trapped total pressure stays constant. The airspeed indicator computes a LARGER dynamic pressure and shows the aircraft speeding up. A pilot who trusts this indication and pulls back to 'slow down' is actually increasing the angle of attack toward a stall while the ASI continues to show increasing speed. A blocked static port freezes the altimeter and VSI and causes the ASI to read low in climbs and high in descents. The alternate static source — cabin air — reads slightly high on all instruments due to the venturi effect of airflow over the fuselage.

**In-flight fire demands immediate, decisive action with zero hesitation.** An electrical fire requires cutting the heat source: Master Switch OFF. The engine continues running on its independent magnetos. After confirming the fire is out, systematic load shedding isolates the faulty circuit by turning breakers on one at a time. An engine fire requires cutting the fuel source: mixture to idle cut-off, fuel selector OFF, fuel pump OFF — then emergency descent and immediate landing. The most dangerous trap with both fire types is the ventilation error: opening a window carelessly creates an aerodynamic vacuum that sucks flames and smoke directly across the pilot's face.

**The startle response is the invisible killer that makes manageable emergencies fatal.** When a sudden, unexpected event occurs, the amygdala hijacks the brain, bypassing logical processing and triggering the fight-flight-freeze response. Cognitive paralysis can last up to 30 seconds — during which the aircraft descends 500 feet with zero pilot input. The most dangerous manifestation is the inappropriate motor response: the instinct to pull back on the yoke to 'get away from the ground,' which stalls the aircraft at the worst possible moment. The antidote is the pre-takeoff verbal briefing, which pre-loads a decision script that short-circuits the freeze response. The PPLA framework — Pitch, Power, Level, Analyze — provides rote physical actions that stabilize the aircraft while the logical brain comes back online.
